nodes.name: MoSe2 solvothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 0.484 g of sodium molybdate (Na2MoO4·2H2O), 0.237 g of Selenium powder (Se), and 0.302 g of Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) were dissolved in 60 mL water in a beaker and then magnetic stirred for 60 min. The resulting homogenous solution was transferred to a 100 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated to 200°C for 24 h. After cooling the solution to room temperature, the achieved precipitate was separated by centrifugation, washed with ethanol, and finally freeze-dried in vacuum for 6 h.

nodes.name: Rh,O-MoSe2-x doping
nodes.procedure: 60 mg of MoSe2 powder was mixed with 60 mL H2O in a round-bottom flask, and the mixture was ultrasonicated for 1 h; then each precursor solution (RhCl3, Alfa Aesar) was added respectively and heated to 90 °C for 12 h. The products were obtained by filtration of the suspension, followed by dialysis in deionized water, and finally dried in a vacuum for 12 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and (Ru, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ possess similar morphologies to MoSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM patterns demonstrate that (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and (Ru, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ possess similar morphologies to MoSe₂ (Figures S4 and S5, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals all samples consist of 2D nanosheets with morphologies well retained after M-O doping; no nanoparticles or clusters observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM patterns (Figures S6 and S7, Supporting Information) further reveal that all samples consist of 2D nanosheets, with the morphologies of MoSe₂ materials well retained after introducing M-O atom pairs.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows ordered MoSe₂ crystalline structure post M-O doping; Rh atoms appear as bright spots homogeneously dispersed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The images show an ordered MoSe₂ crystalline structure after introducing M-O atom pairs, suggesting the atomic dispersion of dopants. Notably, heavier constituent Rh atoms can be discerned within the MoSe₂ matrix (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis reveals that M and O atoms are homogeneously distributed throughout the MoSe₂ backbone.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) analysis reveals that M and O atoms are homogeneously distributed throughout the MoSe₂ backbone (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns indicate that these (M, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ samples possess a trigonal prismatic (2H) structure without any distinct diffraction peaks corresponding to MSeₓ and MOₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns indicate that these (M, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ samples possess a trigonal prismatic (2H) structure without any distinct diffraction peaks corresponding to MSex and MOx (Figure 3a; Figure S11, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra of (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and (Ru, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ exhibit similar characteristics to MoSe₂; introduction of M-O atom pairs may lead to local structural changes and phase evolution manifested in changes near the A1g peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure 3b; Figure S12, Supporting Information) of (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and (Ru, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ exhibit similar characteristics to MoSe₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution Rh 3d XPS shows Rh(II); Ru 2p shows Ru(II); O 1s indicates lattice oxygen with content increasing with Rh loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Rh 3d and Ru 2p XPS spectra (Figures S13 and S14, Supporting Information) reveal that Rh and Ru are expectedly immobilized as Rh (II) and Ru (II) in (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and (Ru, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Rh K-edge XANES shows higher half-edge-step energy vs Rh foil indicating higher Rh oxidation state; Ru K-edge similarly shifted vs Ru foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3d shows the XANES of (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ and Rh foil, revealing a higher energy of the half-edge-step in (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ compared to Rh foil, indicating a higher oxidation state of Rh in (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier transform k³-weighted EXAFS data at Rh K-edge exhibits absence of Rh-Rh scattering peak at 2.74 Å, confirming isolated dispersion of Rh atoms with dominant Rh-Se and Rh-O bonds; coordination numbers of 4.0 (Rh-Se) and 4.3 (Rh-O); for Ru, coordination numbers of 4 (Ru-Se) and 2 (Ru-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform k³-weighted EXAFS data (Figure 3e) at the Rh K³-edge for (Rh, O)-MoSe₂₋ₓ exhibits the absence of the first-shell Rh-Rh scattering peak at 2.74Å, further confirming the isolated dispersion of Rh atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman shows increased intensity of O-H stretching vibrations at 3249 and 3407 cm⁻¹ during HER, indicating enhanced interfacial water adsorption by Rh-O pairs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4f, the variation trends of the two broad bands at 3249 and 3407 cm⁻¹, assignable to tetrahedrally and trihedrally coordinated water at the interface, were analyzed.
